$comment: THE ESTATE PLAN — the single source of the 3D estate map's geometry (DECISIONS.md D-021, D-022).

Nothing here is fact until an element's provenance is "owner-verified", which only the owner's relayed confirmation sets, with the DECISIONS entry that relayed it. The 3D map renders publicly only when every drawn element is owner-verified (src/lib/estate-plan-gate.ts); until then the 2D hotspot map is the page.

Populated 2026-09-14 from the estate's aerial and drone frames by two independent readings, a conservative merge, three adversarial refutations and a final correction. Every value says where it comes from in `basis`; "assumed:" marks what was not observed.

Scale: UNITS: schematic, relative diagram units, NOT metres. No metre conversion is adopted, because pixel-to-metre scales disagree by about 30% between references. No frame has a compass bearing, so bearing = null.

BASE FRAME: proportions were measured on 758a144c at its 2000x1367 display size.
- Reading A: 8.0 display px per unit, origin at display (1017.5, 741).
- Reading B: 7.87 px per unit, origin at (1012, 740.5).
- Merged mapping, used by the merge, refutation and editor passes: x = (iy - 740.75)/7.93 and z = (1014.75 - ix)/7.93. One unit is about 7.93 display px, or 8.9 px on the 2248x1536 original.
- Where a value is a compromise between readings or a combination of observations, its basis is labelled 'derived' and states the rule. 'aerial' is used only where the value is read directly off a frame.

SCALE CHOICE: the compound is the outer wall enclosing the four villas and the walled plot on their sea-ward side.
- Its longer side runs perpendicular to the shore and is roughly 40 units: 37.5 on the lane-side wall and 41.0 on the crop-side wall.
- The two differ because the sea-ward wall runs obliquely: a merge-pass pixel scan of 758a finds it at ix 1152, 1156, 1163 and 1169 at iy 612, 640, 700 and 760.
- Without the walled plot the villa block is about 31.6 x 30 units, so including the plot is what makes the long axis run along z.

ORIGIN: the compound centre. The trapezoid's centroid lies about 0.4 unit inland of the origin, within precision, so the plan is not re-centred.

AXES:
- z is perpendicular to the general shoreline; negative z is sea-ward (image +ix in 758a).
- x is parallel to the general shoreline; negative x is the lane and helipad-apron side (image -iy in 758a).
- Reading A found the chord of the traced shore within about 1.3 degrees of x.
- 0c52 maps to the plan by rotation without mirroring. All passes agree on handedness: the thatched-umbrella cove is on -x, the car park's cove and the row crops on +x.

ORIENTATION: orientation.deg is the rotation of the long axis from +x, counter-clockwise seen from above; +deg turns +x toward -z (the three.js rotation.y sign). Every non-null value is 0 or 90, so the sign convention changes no value.

FOOTPRINT CONVENTIONS:
- {w,d}: when orientation is non-null, w runs along the element's axis and d across it. When orientation is null, w runs along plan x and d along plan z, and the box is only an axis-aligned outline, not a claimed long axis.
- {points}: [x,z] vertices. Compound, apron and venue are closed polygons; lane and shore are open polylines. For point-shapes, position is the centroid or the anchor stated in basis.position.

PRECISION (estimates):
- about ±1 unit for villas and pools; villa footprints are rounded to whole units.
- about ±2-3 for the lane, apron and venue; the helipad centre is ±3 along z, rounded to whole units, and its diameter ±1.5.
- about ±3-5 for the shoreline, whose vertices and anchor are rounded to whole units.
- Lens distortion is not calibrated. The oblique frames (0c52 included) disagree with 758a on some along-strip offsets by several units; see disagreements.

TEXT FIGURES are never used as geometry: 60 m2 indoor area, 20 m2 villa pool, 150 m2 Rituals pool, 97 m2 Rituals specs, 240 m2 estate row, 50 m to the beach.

FRAME FLAG: 758a is flagged in photo-grades.json (g0397) as not attributable. Its match to the estate rests on visual correspondence with the captioned and page frames.

Site states: The frames show at least four states of the site. Capture dates are not established, and neither is the order of the middle states; photo-metrics.json has no date fields, per the prior notes.
- State A (2c985c96): garden newly planted; the compound's walled sea-ward plot planted in rows; a terracotta, bougainvillea-covered building on the later Rituals site; a paved apron with no H.
- State B (758a144c, 12e099d0): the Rituals pool terrace is built; the apron is an unmarked paved yard with trucks and cars and no H. 12e0's order relative to 758a and to state C is unknown.
- State C (0c52479b = ritual-drone-1, fe9ae318, 84d095ea, 9a16ab0a, Ritual-drone = thalasses-all-2, Helipad-2s): the yellow H circle is painted on the apron, a see-through post-and-brace fence with a gate runs along the apron's lane edge, and a paved lower plaza lies sea-ward of the venue pool.
- State D (01e51076): as state C, plus a new white flat-roofed building directly landward of the venue pool.

Combinations made in this plan, stated openly:
1. State B (758a) supplies the compound, villas, villa pools, lane, Rituals terrace, Rituals pool and shoreline (including the rock tongue). The Rituals venue outline is now single-state: it ends at the 758a terrace wall, and the state-C lower plaza is not drawn.
2. The helipad (state C) is placed along the strip by comparing the H centre directly with the compound's lane-side sea-ward wall end, a feature constant across states, in the state-C frames (0c52, 84d0, 9a16, fe9a, Ritual-drone). Across the strip it uses state-C across-apron ratios applied to the apron outline below. Its diameter is a state-C ratio applied to that outline.
3. The apron polygon is the state-B yard (758a) for its landward and lane-side edges, combined with H-state proportions for its sea-ward limit and far edge. It is not the state-C apron: 0c52 and 84d0 suggest the state-C landward edge lies nearer z -12.5 to -13. The helipad is not positioned by ratio on this outline.

Not drawn:
- the state-A planted plot (the vegetable-garden match fits only state A)
- the state-D white building
- the state-C venue lower plaza
- Villa Pueblo

Constant across states: the compound walls, the four villas and their pool slots, and the lane, in every frame checked.

frame.orientation: orientation.deg turns an element's long axis from +x, counter-clockwise seen from above (+deg turns +x toward -z); null when not established

basis.footprint: aerial: 758a — inland wall ix≈855 (z +20.0); lane-side wall iy≈613-616 (x -15.8); crop-side wall iy≈866-868 (x +15.8). Sea-ward wall: a merge-pass pixel scan finds it running ix 1152→1169 between iy 612 and 760 and reaching about ix 1181 at the crop-side wall, so z ≈ -17.5 at the lane-side end and -21.0 at the crop-side end. elements.notes:
The name uses the source's wording for this enclosure, 'the complex' of four villas. The site applies 'Thalasses Villas' to a five-villa brand that includes Villa Pueblo (inventory.md:125; en__property__2142.txt:63; en__villa-pueblo-1.txt:52), and this outline does not include Pueblo, so that name is not used here.

The outline is the outer wall, including the walled plot. The villa block (villas, pools, central garden, playground, carports) runs from z +20 to a hedge line at about z -10.2 (A -9.4, B -11). The walled plot lies between that hedge and the oblique sea-ward wall.

Around the outline: the carports and entrance lawn sit at the +x inland corner, and the lane rounds the -x inland corner. A dirt track and row crops border the +x wall, and a dry field lies between the sea-ward wall and the car park. Neither is part of this outline.

Between x -22 and -4 the averaged traces had followed the sand line at the base of the rock tongue. Villas' private beach 50m

sources: src/app/home-data.ts:219 (redesign label 'The private beach', not used)
elements.notes:
The shore is two coves with rock between them.
- Cove (a), -x side: thatched umbrellas around x -72 to -62, reached by a straight path.
- Between cove (a) and the tongue: a partly submerged reef shelf (x about -40 to -15). The venue stands landward of it.
- The emergent rock tongue (x -15..-6, to z about -106): sea-ward of the car park, on the venue's +x side.
- Cove (b), +x side: sandy, with bathers, sea-ward of the compound. Its waterline runs from the tongue's base (x about -4) toward +x, past the dirt car park at the lane's end (B: x -17 to +1, z -56 to -72).

The polyline is clipped to 758a's frame, and both beaches continue beyond it. The name is descriptive: 'private beach' is kept only in stated. The '50m' figures are text and are not reconciled with the layout, which puts the waterline about 75-100 units sea-ward of the sea-side villas.

elements.name: Private Helipad

basis.identity: aerial: a painted yellow H in a circle on the apron in 0c52, fe9a, 9a16, 84d0, 01e5, Ritual-drone and Helipad-2s; absent in 758a, 12e0 and 2c98. text: page title 'Private Helipad' (content/text/en__private-helipad-1.txt:1). The caption 'Thalasses Villas - Private Helipad' (content/captions.json:653) is repeated on eight entries (:653-688), so it labels the album, not each image.
basis.position:
derived, cross-state.
- Along the strip (z): the H centre is measured directly against the compound's lane-side sea-ward wall end (z -17.5), a feature constant across states, in each state-C frame. 0c52: about 3-4.5 units sea-ward of it (wall end at about 0.25 of the apron length from its landward edge, H centre at about 0.48). 84d0: about 2 sea-ward. 9a16: level to about 3 sea-ward. fe9a: roughly level. Ritual-drone (strong oblique): about 4 landward. Adopted z about -20 (±3).
- Across the strip (x): the H centre sits about 0.47-0.54 of the apron width from its lane edge (0c52, fe9a, 84d0). Per-frame values are -30.5 (0c52), -33.3 (fe9a), about -32 (84d0) and about -33.5 (9a16). On the corrected apron outline at z -20 (lane edge about -21.8, far edge -42.8) this gives about -32.
- Rounded to whole units. Not placed by an along-strip ratio on the state-B apron outline.
basis.orientation: aerial: 0c52, fe9a, 9a16, 84d0 — the H's two long strokes run across the walled strip (parallel to the shore, plan x) and its crossbar runs along the strip. In 0c52 one column through the centre crosses two separate yellow bands (iy 245-250 and 275-280); in 84d0 the yellow bbox (170 x 82 px) is elongated across the strip; in 9a16 the strokes run parallel to the apron's landward fence line. deg applies to the painted glyph; the circle itself has no axis.
basis.footprint:
derived: circle diameter as a fraction of the apron. Readings:
- A: 0.58 of the apron width (0c52) and 0.57 of its length (fe9a) → 12.5.
- B's own ratio (apron width / 1.75 on its 22.5-wide apron) → about 12.9. B's stated 10 is inconsistent with it.
- merge-pass read of fe9a: 0.59-0.61 → 12.0-13.5.
- layout refutation pass, 0c52: 0.57 of the width.
Rule: A's value, which lies inside the merge-read range and below B's ratio. Precision ±1.5. w = d = the diameter.

elements.name: Helipad apron (no site name on record)

basis.position: derived: centroid of the polygon below.
basis.orientation: not-established: its sides run parallel to the strip and compound walls, but it is near-square (about 21-23 by 20), so it has no long axis.
basis.footprint:
derived, cross-state: the state-B yard (758a) for the landward and lane-side edges, combined with H-state proportions for the sea-ward limit and far edge.
- Landward edge: 758a A z -6.2 (ix≈1067), B -8 (ix 1077) → -7.1. This is the state-B yard; 0c52 and 84d0 suggest the state-C apron's landward edge lies near -12.5 to -13, which is not adopted.
- Sea-ward limit at the white planter structures: A -26.6, B -27 (set from H-state ratios) → -26.8.
- Lane-side edge: -19.5 at the landward end. At the sea-ward end it is moved from -20.5 to -23.5 so the apron clears the lane (the lane centreline is about -21.1 there and the lane about 4 wide). This matches a faint kerb in 758a running from about x -19.3 at z -10 to about -23.7 at z -26.8.
- Far edge: A -43.5 (a blend of 758a -42.3 and 0c52 about -45), B -42 → -42.8.
The helipad is not positioned by ratio on this outline.

elements.notes: A service yard with white planter structures and a paved court (z about -26.8 to -45) joins the apron to the Rituals terrace; it is not drawn as a separate element. The outline mixes the pre-H yard (758a) with H-state proportions (see site_state_note). The lane edge is fenced in state C, not open and not walled. The site text names the pad ('heli-pad'), not the apron, so the name here is descriptive.

State D (01e5) adds a white building landward of the pool inside this outline, which is not drawn. DECISIONS.md:582 lists the Rituals venue's position as waiting on the site plan.

elements.name: Lane (no site name on record)

basis.identity: aerial: 758a, 0c52, fe9a, 84d0, 9a16, 12e0, Ritual-drone, 2c98, 01e5 — the paved lane. It arrives from inland, runs along the compound's inland wall, rounds its lane-side inland corner and runs along the lane-side wall. It then passes the fenced lane edge of the apron (a see-through post-and-brace fence with a gate in state C) and the strip's lane-side wall, and ends at the car park by cove (b).
basis.position: derived: the point where the centreline passes level with the origin; A -17.5, B -18. The layout refutation pass confirmed the inland run on a grid-overlaid 758a crop.
basis.orientation: aerial: 758a, Ritual-drone, 84d0 — the main run beside the compound is parallel to z. Past the compound it deflects toward -x (see disagreements); the bends are carried only in the points.
basis.footprint:
derived: centreline.
- Inland end: vertices averaged between A's 11 and B's 7, each reading interpolated at the other's z (or x on the inland run). A merge-pass crop confirms the approach road from inland at about x +7 to +9, the turn at the compound's +x inland corner (display ≈847,800), the run along the inland wall at z ≈21-22 and the turn round the lane-side inland corner (≈852,623). The first vertex is A's point on the approach road.
- Beyond z -30: both traces had followed the dry field's boundary wall, which is the lane's +x edge (x -20.4 at z -30.7, -23.3 at -43.3, -23.5 at -61.6; layout refutation pass on a 758a crop). Those vertices are moved about 1.5-2 units toward -x, to the middle of the paved lane between that wall and the service-yard/venue lane-side wall (x -26.1 at z -34 to -27.5 at z -68).
- The last vertex moves the same way, from between A (-18.9,-75.3) and B (-25.5,-72) to about (-24.5,-73.7).

elements.notes:
The points trace the centreline. The lane is about 2.2-2.5 units wide beside the compound and about 3-4.5 units wide beyond it.

Beside the compound it runs between the lane-side wall (x -15.8) and the apron's lane edge (x -19.5 at the landward end to -23.5 at the sea-ward end). That edge is a see-through fence with a gate in state C, not an open edge and not a solid wall. Further sea-ward it runs between the dry field's wall and the service-yard/venue lane-side wall.

At its inland end it continues beyond the first vertex to a main road outside the plan. A separate dirt track runs along the compound's +x wall; it is not this lane. The site text gives no name, so the name is descriptive.
